Priya (ML Eng): Heads-up: brought up Aquila-10B on int6 and int4 profiles for a mixed customer chat workload. Short summary below — surprising fidelity on int4 for one-shot prompts but degradation shows up on multi-step planning.

Diego (Quant): Nice. Numbers?

Priya (ML Eng): Baseline = fp16, experiments int6 (symmetric) and int4 (blocked). Dataset: 6k sampled chats (mix of short chit-chat, instruction tasks, and 2-6 turn planning). Key aggregates:
- latency p95 fp16 320ms, int6 260ms, int4 230ms
- throughput per GPU: fp16 36 tok/s, int6 46 tok/s, int4 58 tok/s
- ROUGE-L (planning slices) fp16 0.64, int6 0.62, int4 0.55
- one-shot factual exact-match fp16 0.71, int6 0.70, int4 0.69
- top1 human pref (blind A/B, n=600): fp16 48%, int6 45%, int4 39% (fp16 vs int4 statistically significant)
- cost per 1M tokens (incl infra overhead) fp16 $8.00, int6 $5.75, int4 $3.80

Nina (Product): So int4 gets big cost wins but hurts multi-step planning a lot. Which user cohorts rely on planning?

Priya (ML Eng): Internal slice breakdown: planning-heavy sessions ~12% of traffic but ~28% of token consumption (longer context). Chit-chat short sessions are ~58% of sessions but low tokens.

Kai (SRE): Operationally int4 uses ~40% less GPU memory, letting us fit 1.4x GPUs worth of capacity per node. That means effective per-token infra cost drops similarly. Also watch for numerical instabilities causing rare NaN traces — we saw 3/10k requests hit postprocessing exceptions on int4 in staging.

EvalBot: Quick automated slice snapshot:
```
slice: short-chat (n=3500)
  fp16: metric=0.88
  int6: metric=0.87
  int4: metric=0.86
slice: multi-step-planning (n=700)
  fp16: metric=0.64
  int6: metric=0.62
  int4: metric=0.55
```

Diego (Quant): Hypothesis: int4 quant introduces stepwise error accumulation across decoder timesteps for planning sequences. We should run per-token perplexity drift and per-head MSE vs fp16 on planning traces. Also compare KV-cache scale factors.

Priya (ML Eng): Routing thought: three-tier hybrid. Keep fp16 for planning-flagged sessions or long context (>1024 tokens) -> int6 for medium length or numeric-sensitive tasks -> int4 as cost-optimized fallback for short, stateless interactions. Proposed guard features: planning_flag (from client intent), prompt_len, and token_budget.

Nina (Product): Product constraints: Search and summarization pipelines are strict — no more than 1% drop on ROUGE-like metrics tolerated. For consumer chat, 2-3% drop might be acceptable given price improvements but need A/B. What's monthly $ impact if we route 50% of short sessions to int4?

Priya (ML Eng): Back-of-envelope:
```
avg_tokens_per_session = 900
short_session_fraction = 0.58
short_session_tokens = avg_tokens_per_session * short_session_fraction ~= 522
if 50% short -> tokens_moved_per_user = 522 * 0.5 = 261 tokens/day/user
savings_per_token = (5.75-3.80)/1e6 = 0.00000195 $/token approx
daily_save_per_user ~= 261 * 0.00000195 ~= $0.000509
per_1M_DAU_day ~= $509/day (~$15.3k/mo)
```
Caveats: excludes costs for increased monitoring, user-unhappy remediation, and potential revenue loss.

Kai (SRE): Canary plan: small staged rollout over 3 phases: staging smoke -> 1% user traffic (short only) 48h -> 10% short turns 72h -> 25% short turns 7d. Metrics to auto-fail: production error spike >0.3%, planning-slice ROUGE drop >0.8 absolute, human-pref drop >2 pts. Rollback immediate on fail.

Diego (Quant): Action items:
1) Per-token drift experiment for planning traces (n>=1k long trajectories).
2) Head-wise MSE & KV-scale audit for int4 quant params.
3) Small perturbation test: re-run int4 with bias correction layer (calibrated) to see if planning loss recovers.

Priya (ML Eng): I'll queue the drift/perturbation jobs tonight and prepare a lightweight scorecard template (48h snapshot + 7d follow-up).

Nina (Product): Approve 1% short-only canary. Product will hold on broad 10% until quant fixes / calibrations show planning-slice within 0.8 points of fp16. Please ping me with the scorecard.

Priya (ML Eng): Thanks — will update thread with the 48h scorecard and attach logs for any NaN exceptions.

EvalBot: Note: created eval-run id=eval-4933333333-1 for automated comparison.
